title: Signalboard
summary: Real-time ops dashboard for a distributed worker fleet, with live status and incident timelines.
body:
Signalboard started as a weekend prototype for monitoring background jobs and grew into the daily ops surface for a small platform team. The hard part was not the charts — it was keeping the UI calm while events arrive in bursts.

I built a typed event stream, a compact incident timeline, and URL-persisted filters so on-call engineers can share exact views. Latency stayed under a few hundred milliseconds on a modest VPS.

architecture.label: Client
architecture.detail: Next.js ops UI with URL-synced filters and a calm incident timeline.

architecture.label: Realtime
architecture.detail: Typed WebSocket event stream driven by worker fleet heartbeats.

architecture.label: API
architecture.detail: Node handlers normalize events and aggregate incident data.

architecture.label: DB
architecture.detail: Postgres stores incidents, worker state, and timeline slices.

architecture.label: Workers
architecture.detail: Distributed job runners emit status and failure signals.

title: Ledger Lite
summary: Personal finance CLI and web companion that imports CSVs and reconciles categories without requiring a bank login.
body:
Ledger Lite keeps financial data local. A CLI parses bank CSVs, a small web UI reviews categories, and everything syncs through a local SQLite file.

The interesting design choice was treating the CLI as the source of truth and the web app as a review surface — less magic, easier audits.

architecture.label: CLI
architecture.detail: TypeScript importer parses CSVs and writes categorized rows.

architecture.label: Web UI
architecture.detail: Review surface for category corrections and monthly views.

architecture.label: tRPC
architecture.detail: Typed procedures between the UI and local Node process.

architecture.label: SQLite
architecture.detail: Single-file ledger — the source of truth stays on disk.
